title: Work IQ: retrieve tool gives agents Microsoft 365 grounding content
summary: The roadmap details, preview retrieval behaviour, Copilot Credits billing and documented controls are supported. Minor corrections should complete the spending-policy navigation, simplify the Graph call, acknowledge the documented workIQ service category and remove checklist controls that have no table row.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn describes retrieve as available in public preview, separately from the roadmap's In development status.
claims.quote: The `retrieve` tool is available in public preview.

claims.claim: Source metadata can include sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: `sensitivityLabel` | object | Sensitivity-label metadata for the source, when available.

claims.claim: Source metadata can include a contentProtection evaluation value.
claims.quote: `contentProtection` | string | The content-protection evaluation result, when available.

claims.quote: Don't treat a missing, failed, blocked, or unrecognized value as an allow decision.

claims.claim: Developers have responsibility for how the retrieving application uses source security metadata.
claims.quote: Use `results` for programmatic operations such as: ... Applying application-specific redaction or filtering. ... Inspecting sensitivity-label metadata.

claims.claim: Work IQ uses delegated authentication.

claims.claim: Retrieve requires a registered client application with the delegated WorkIQAgent.Ask permission.
claims.quote: Register a client application and grant the delegated `WorkIQAgent.Ask` permission.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Scope; controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Calling users need usage-based billing and assignment to a spending policy that includes Work IQ API.
claims.quote: Set up usage-based billing for Copilot Credits and assign the calling users to a spending policy that includes Work IQ API.

claims.claim: Where an organisation uses Work IQ MCP policy, Learn requires confirming Work IQ MCP is enabled.
claims.quote: If your organization uses Work IQ MCP policy, confirm that Work IQ MCP is enabled.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The retrieve capability is admin-opt-in because access requires billing setup, spending-policy coverage and consent.
claims.quote: Set up usage-based billing for Copilot Credits and assign the calling users to a spending policy that includes Work IQ API. ... Register a client application and grant the delegated `WorkIQAgent.Ask` permission.

claims.where: Why it matters; Open questions: policy default
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether the tenant-level Work IQ MCP policy is on or off by default.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP policy default enabled; Work IQ retrieve default admin enable. Read policy-governance-mcp, retrieve, MCP overview and enable-work-iq; mutation defaults are stated, but the tenant policy toggle's default is not.

claims.claim: Retrieve is a read-style grounding tool rather than a data-mutation operation.
claims.quote: Entity tools ... CRUD operations and actions ... Copilot tools | `ask`, `retrieve`, `list_agents` | Invoke Microsoft 365 Copilot, retrieve grounding content, and discover available agents

claims.claim: The Work IQ MCP policy documentation says create, update, delete and modifying action requests are blocked by default.
claims.quote: By default, mutation operations aren't allowed for safety. This restriction includes create, update, delete, and action requests that modify data, such as sending email.

claims.claim: Administrators can enable supported mutation scenarios through tenant policy.
claims.quote: Administrators can enable supported mutation scenarios through tenant policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center when those capabilities are needed.

claims.claim: The policy page does not describe the mutation restriction as behaviour specific to retrieve.
claims.quote: Searched: retrieve and mutation in policy-governance-mcp and tool-reference. The former gives a general modifying-operation restriction; the latter describes retrieve separately as returning grounding.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Learn says tool availability and schemas can evolve and instructs clients to discover the retrieve schema through tools/list.
claims.quote: Call `tools/list` after connecting and confirm that `retrieve` is available. Tool availability and schemas can evolve, so use the schema returned by `tools/list` as the source of truth

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: A Work IQ MCP policy change can take up to 24 hours to apply across the tenant.
claims.quote: After you save the setting, it can take up to 24 hours for the policy change to apply across your tenant.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; summary; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Work IQ API uses consumption licensing billed in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: You pay for use of the Work IQ API through a usage-based model that uses Copilot Credits.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Work IQ API access is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing.
claims.quote: Work IQ API access is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing and available through usage-based billing.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Work IQ API consumes Copilot Credits shared with other eligible services.
claims.quote: Work IQ API usage consumes Copilot Credits shared with other eligible services.

claims.claim: Prepaid credits and pay-as-you-go can fund consumption for Work IQ API and other supported services such as Cowork.
claims.quote: Depending on the service, organizations can use ... pay-as-you-go billing, prepaid capacity packs, or supported combinations ... Services ... now include: ... Cowork ... Work IQ API for custom apps and agents

claims.claim: Spending policies define access and spending limits without reserving or allocating Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Spending policies are limit-based controls and don't reserve or allocate Copilot Credits to users or groups.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Auto-apply new services is on by default for spending policies and automatically adds newly supported services.
claims.quote: By default, the **Auto-apply new services** toggle is selected for spending policies. ... When the setting is on, newly supported Microsoft Copilot services and agents are automatically added to the policy.

claims.claim: Consumption through custom integrations that call Work IQ directly appears under Work IQ API.
claims.quote: Coding agents or custom integrations that call Work IQ directly: Consumption through that connection appears under Work IQ API.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Cost varies because one request can involve multiple tool calls and reasoning steps.
claims.quote: One user request can involve multiple tool calls and reasoning steps. Work IQ includes deterministic operations and variable-cost contextual reasoning, so a prompt isn't necessarily a single fixed-price operation.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No Copilot Credit rate specific to retrieve or its strategies is documented in the Microsoft Learn billing and feature material checked.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ retrieve Copilot Credits rate pricing grounding copilot meter; Work IQ retrieve rate licensing. Read retrieve, tool-reference, Work IQ overview, API overview, usage-based billing overview and Business Applications costs; results give no retrieve-specific rate.

claims.claim: Work IQ API does not support application-only authentication.
claims.quote: Application-only authentication isn't supported.

claims.claim: The Work IQ MCP policy is reached in Microsoft 365 admin center through Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select **Agents** > **Tools**. ... select **Work IQ MCP**. ... select the **Policy** tab when it's available.

claims.where: summary; controls[0].governs; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Tenant policy can allow or deny Work IQ MCP requests, including retrieve requests.
claims.quote: Don't automatically retry a policy-denied request. Policy denials require the user or an administrator to review access, consent, billing assignment, or Work IQ MCP policy.

claims.claim: The initial Work IQ MCP policy surface is tenant-level, without per-user, per-app, per-agent or scenario-specific policy templates.
claims.quote: Tenant-level control applies across the tenant. Per-user, per-app, per-agent, or scenario-specific policy templates aren't part of the initial policy control surface.

claims.claim: No API for reading or changing the tenant Work IQ MCP policy is documented in the Microsoft material checked.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP policy API update policy settings Graph tenant retrieve; Work IQ policy PATCH. Read policy-governance-mcp, tool-reference, MCP overview and returned Graph references; no operation for the MCP policy was returned.

claims.claim: Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > + Add spending policy reaches the spending-policy creation workflow in Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: go to **Copilot > Cost Management**. ... Select the **Configuration** tab and then select **+ Add spending policy**. ... Define the policy scope ... Select agents and services ... Set limits and alerts
claims.fix: The path stops at the correct workflow but not its limits. Replace controls[1].ui.path and the rendered route with 'Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > + Add spending policy > Policy scope > Identity > Select agents and services > Set limits and alerts'. Keep the note that Work IQ API must be selected. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-manage-copilot-credits.

claims.claim: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} updates periodLimit, perUserLimit or billingMethods with an If-Match ETag header.
claims.quote: PATCH /copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} ... If-Match | The ETag of the spending policy. Required. ... The following properties can be updated: `displayName`, `periodLimit`, `perUserLimit`, and `billingMethods`.
claims.fix: Set controls[1].api.call and the rendered call to 'PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}'. Add to the row note: 'The request body sets periodLimit or perUserLimit to change spending limits; If-Match supplies the policy ETag.' Leave complete billingMethods change requirements to the linked reference.

claims.claim: The update-spending-policy API requires CopilotCostManagement-Policy.ReadWrite.All.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | CopilotCostManagement-Policy.ReadWrite.All

claims.claim: The Copilot Cost Management API is beta and unsupported for production applications.
claims.quote: APIs under the `/beta` version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: No page checked identifies the API's service settings specifically with the individual Work IQ API billable service.
claims.quote: Searched: spendingPolicyServiceSetting workIQ Work IQ API serviceSettings. Read spendingpolicyservicesetting: serviceId identifies a category such as workIQ; multiple billable services can share a category. No individual Work IQ API mapping is stated.
claims.fix: Replace 'This briefing found no page saying that API's service settings expose Work IQ API specifically.' with 'The API documents a governed-service category named workIQ; multiple billable services can share a category.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/cost-management/resources/spendingpolicyservicesetting. Do not equate the category with an individual billable service.

claims.where: Governance controls: final paragraph; Open questions: source restriction
claims.claim: Capabilities and strategy are request parameters, not documented tenant-admin enforcement settings for retrieve source types.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP policy API tenant retrieve source restrictions. Read retrieve, tool-reference and policy-governance-mcp: capabilities is a source allow list for one request; no tenant-level retrieve source-type setting is documented.

claims.claim: Spending policies support monthly policy and optional per-user limits, and users reaching a limit lose access until credits reset.
claims.quote: When users hit the limit, they lose access to agents and services for the rest of the month until credits reset on the first of the month. ... Select monthly budget limits for users (optional).

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center Cost management dashboard lets administrators review Work IQ API consumption.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft admin center, **Copilot > Cost management**, admins can monitor Copilot Credit consumption and manage spending associated with the supported services such as ... **Work IQ API**.
